title: Multi-tier cache and stampede protection
prerequisites: Expiry and eviction introduced in this scenario
learning_objectives: Propose and revise an inspectable architecture
problem_statement: Design a read-through experience for an expensive database lookup. Explain how many requests reach the origin when a popular cached key expires.

progressive_constraints.title: Dictionary cache
progressive_constraints.description: Identify cached state and the authoritative data source.

progressive_constraints.title: Origin budget
progressive_constraints.description: Compute origin reads from declared miss fraction and compare with the origin read budget.

progressive_constraints.title: Hot-key expiry
progressive_constraints.description: Ten thousand simultaneous misses must not cause ten thousand expensive origin refreshes.

progressive_constraints.title: Write race
progressive_constraints.description: A refresh races with a write and invalidation. Declare a version/lease/ordering mechanism and a staleness bound.

valid_architecture_families.name: Look-aside cache with singleflight
valid_architecture_families.description: Application tier coalesces misses and uses an explicit invalidation/version policy.

valid_architecture_families.name: Write-through with leases
valid_architecture_families.description: Writes and refreshes use versioned leases to prevent stale overwrite.

valid_architecture_families.name: Edge cache with origin shield
valid_architecture_families.description: Stale-while-revalidate and a shared shield bound fan-in while honoring a declared staleness window.

common_misconceptions: A cache is not a source of truth merely because it is fast.
Expiry synchronizes demand unless refreshes are coalesced.
Delete-after-write alone does not prevent every stale refresh race.

hint_ladder.level_1: Count the origin requests when all callers miss the same key.
hint_ladder.level_2: Compare waiting behind one refresh with serving a bounded stale value.
hint_ladder.level_3: If 10000 callers share one refresh, origin fan-in is one for that key; it is not a 10000x load spike. A lease/version check prevents an older refresh from overwriting a newer value.

consolidation: Cache design includes miss behavior, coalescing, write ordering and the permitted staleness window. The linked DSA exercise teaches dictionary reasoning, not an implemented LRU cache.
fresh_transfer_question: What changes if the cached value is an account balance that must be immediately fresh after a write?
coach_instructions: One clear question at a time. Inspect actual graph and stated assumptions. Do not grade prose by keywords or require a vendor name. Numeric assumptions are learner declarations, not measured performance. Explain when asked, require teach-back, and preserve alternative valid designs. Do not silently edit the diagram.
